subject: Recap + next steps: on-prem/VPC economics and license options
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap + next steps: on-prem/VPC economics and license options

Hi Jane — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can put together a clean pricing packet and SOW for Acme Health.

Call highlights (as I captured them):
- Primary use: clinical documentation enhancement across 3 app surfaces (clinician notes, intake forms, transcription post-processing).
- Expected steady-state usage: roughly 50M–200M tokens/month initially, with peak batch jobs pushing another ~50M in month-end processing.
- Deployment preference: Private VPC in AWS GovCloud for PHI scope; potential on-prem for one pilot hospital later.
- Environments: dev + staging + prod initially (3), with potential to add a separate pilot environment per hospital (up to 6 total).
- Security/compliance needs: SOC2 evidence, KMS integration, audit logs retention (7 years asked by compliance team).

Open questions for you (to finalize pricing):
1) Target annual budget range for platform + support? A rough band (e.g., $30k–$80k, $80k–$200k) helps us tailor license vs committed token pricing.
2) Do you prefer a subscription license (platform fee + token consumption) vs. an enterprise perpetual-style license with annual support?
3) Any hard $/1M tokens target you have internally we should try to hit? We commonly see benchmarks teams target between $500–$3,000 per 1M tokens depending on on-prem vs hosted and support SLAs — curious where Acme lands.

Next steps from our side once we have answers:
- Build 2 proposal options: (A) subscription with committed monthly tokens + standard support, and (B) enterprise license with multi-environment pricing and priority support.
- Include unit economics (expected $/1M tokens) under each scenario and an example year 1 cost at low/mid/high usage.
- Deliver SOW draft and pricing packet (will include attachments: pricing summary + SOW template).

I’ll aim to send the packet by EOD tomorrow once you confirm budget band and environment count.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
D: +1 415-555-0126
redwood.ai

From: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acmehealth.com>

Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps: on-prem/VPC economics and license options

Thanks, Dylan — that was helpful and matches how we saw the call. Quick answers below: 

1) Budget band: for year 1 we can commit to a $75k–$150k range, with flexibility if price/performance is demonstrated in the pilot. Procurement prefers a committed spend if unit economics are favorable.
2) Preference: procurement leans toward subscription (term license) with committed tokens and an option to convert to a term-based perpetual license in year 2. But our engineering/security leads are open to an on-prem perpetual if it materially reduces unit cost.
3) Target $/1M tokens: our internal target is roughly $1,200 per 1M tokens for production traffic. For batch/analytics tokens we can accept a higher rate.

Environment count: start with 3 (dev/stage/prod). If pilot hospital #1 goes well we expect to add 2–3 dedicated pilot envs next quarter (so plan for up to 6).

Compliance: we need SOC2 + KMS + proof of isolation for the prod env.

If you can send scenario A (subscription committed tokens) and B (enterprise on-prem term) with sample costs at low/mid/high usage, that will be perfect.

—Jane
Jane Doe
Head of Clinical AI 
Acme Health

Subject: RE: Recap + next steps: on-prem/VPC economics and license options

Hi Jane — thanks for the clarity. Inline quick pricing assumptions so expectations align before we produce the packet:

Assumptions:
- Production profile: 100M tokens/month (mid) steady-state for example calculations.
- Pilot batch spikes: +50M tokens (month-end).
- 3 primary envs; option to add up to 3 pilot envs later.

Scenario A — Subscription (recommended for flexibility):
- Platform fee: $12k/year base for private VPC (management/control plane + baseline SLAs)
- Committed token tiers: 0–50M @ $2,500/1M tokens; 50–200M @ $1,100/1M tokens; 200M+ negotiate enterprise slab
- Support: Standard (business hours, 24h escalation) included; Premium (24x7 with named TAM) is +20–30% uplift on platform fee and per-token price improvements.
- Example (100M mo): annual = platform $12k + token spend (100M @ blended $1,300 = $130k) => ~$142k/yr (ex. integration fees, setup).

Scenario B — Enterprise/on-prem (lower unit price, higher upfront):
- One-time license fee for on-prem runtime + compilation kernels: $85k–$150k depending on environment count and binary distribution model.
- Annual support & maintenance: 18% of license (~$15k–$27k/yr) for Standard; Premium (onsite + 4 hr SLA) +30% on top.
- Token pricing: typically $700–$1,000/1M depending on committed volumes and whether we run in your data center vs. Redwood-managed private VPC.
- Example (100M mo typical): if on-prem license chosen and we price tokens at $900/1M => 100M/mo = $1,080k/yr token compute + support; but often customers choose to buy larger license bundles / reserved capacity which reduces token compute cost — we’ll model a 1–3 year amortized view.

Notes: the biggest driver is environment topology (multi-tenant vs isolated envs) and whether Redwood manages the private VPC. Isolated single-tenant envs increase OPEX by ~10–25%.

We’ll produce a one-page comparison table plus year-1 cost scenarios at low/mid/high usage and include unit economics ($/1M tokens) under each. Any objections to these ranges?

-Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>

Subject: RE: Recap + next steps: on-prem/VPC economics and license options

Adding a technical lens for environment and support impact on price: 

- Environment count: dev/stage/prod (3) is straightforward. If Acme requests an additional per-hospital isolated pilot environment, we treat those as separate isolated deployments. Each isolated env requires its own infra reservation (or tenancy) and adds ~8–12% cost per env. If you prefer shared multi-tenant pilot namespaces we can save ~40% on the incremental cost.
- Data residency & KMS: for GovCloud we provide KMS integration; HSM integrations are treated as a professional service with an estimated 3–6 week engagement.
- Audit logs retention: 7-year retention increases storage and egress considerations; we'll model it as a fixed $X/month per env in the packet (we typically see $400–$1,200/mo per env depending on volume).
- Performance SLOs: Premium support + priority capacity reservation (useful for clinical peaks) requires reserved capacity commitments (monthly GPU pool commit) — this is priced as an annual reserved pool, not per-token, and materially lowers peak-unit cost.

Happy to put together a quick spreadsheet that maps environment choices to estimated license/support/token-price outcomes.

—Rishi
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Jane — thanks for the quick replies and team input. Attached are: (1) a 1-page pricing comparison PDF and (2) a draft SOW that maps environments and timelines. Highlights from the packet: 

- Subscription (Scenario A) sample (100M mo): ~$142k/yr (mid) — blended token $/1M ~ $1,300.
- Enterprise on-prem sample (100M mo): large upfront license amortized reduces token compute but increases year-1 cash (we show amortized 36-mo and 12-mo views). For modeling, token unit ~$900/1M in on-prem reserved pool with 18% annual support.
- Premium support / reserved capacity option reduces peak-unit cost by ~25% vs pay-as-you-go token pricing.
- We flagged SOC2 + KMS + audit retention items; timeline to delivery for GovCloud private VPC: ~6 weeks to baseline deploy, 8–10 weeks to complete HSM / bespoke security work.

Next steps / asks: 
1) Procurement: confirm whether procurement needs a PO to attach to the draft SOW or if you prefer an MSA first.
2) Jane / Eng: confirm whether pilot envs will be isolated per hospital or shared namespace (impacts costs).
3) We will schedule a short walk-through of the packet with your procurement/security on Thursday 8/6 — does 10:00 AM PT work?

I’ll upload the final packet to the HubSpot record and share a drive link. Let me know if you want any of the numbers adjusted before the walk-through.

Best regards,
